added_provisions.reason: Rule (27) of section 31 was in force at the October 2020 reference date and is the rule written for a deed that two or more parties are to execute but that only one has signed. It requires the notary who took the first signature to return the part-executed deed in his monthly list, to produce the duplicate on the Registrar of Lands' notice, and to deliver the duplicate to the registrar if the deed is still unsigned by all parties three months after it was first signed. Question 1 proposes precisely such a staged execution and the map recorded no time limit on it. Added as supporting for M065-Q01.

The map cited only section 32(2)(i), which fixes one date for rules (6), (7), (23) and (25). Paragraph (ii) is the one that governs rules (18) and (20), and it is what tells the first notary which day and place to state under rule (20)(c) when the parties sign at different times. Section 32 was not attached to M065-Q02 at all. Added as supporting for M065-Q02.

The scenario turns on who is known to which notary, and the map's only rule (9) entry (PROV-M065-022) quotes the post-2022 identification wording, which was not in force in October 2020. The repealed wording is recited verbatim in Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(6) and is therefore quotable from this corpus, which makes the identification point in question 1 rest on matter-date text. Added as supporting for M065-Q01.

Rule (22), the pivot of question 1, forbids attestation outside the area "in which he is authorized to practice" but does not say what fixes that area. Section 2 of the Notaries Ordinance does: the warrant specifies the area and the language. The map had no provision supplying this definition. Added as background for M065-Q01.

question_decisions.note: The route the answer takes (two-stage execution before two notaries under section 31 rule (25) read with section 32(2)) is fully carried by the corpus text, and every indispensable provision was confirmed verbatim and unamended at October 2020. Nothing in the answer needs Roman-Dutch law or a decided case. Held at proposed_gold. Two qualifications for the lawyer: the only entry that is post-date, PROV-M065-008, is supporting rather than indispensable, and the background is internally ambiguous about who is lessor and who is lessee, though the analysis does not turn on it.

The block is correct and I confirmed its basis directly: No. 31 of 2022 s.16(11)(a) and (b) repeal and substitute rule (20)(b) and (e) without reciting the repealed words, and s.16(11)(d) inserts paragraph (h). The question asks for a list of the contents of an attestation, so completeness is the whole answer and it cannot be given for October 2020 from this corpus. All six indispensable provisions were separately confirmed unamended at the matter date, so the block is narrow: only the identification item and the consideration item are missing. A point-in-time 2020 edition of the Ordinance would clear it.

disagreements.researcher_position: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 (PROV-M065-008) is post-matter-date text throughout, so applicable_to_matter_date is false and the provision can only be supporting.
disagreements.verifier_position: The words the map actually quotes are the opening scope words of section 2, including the carve-out for a lease at will or for a period not exceeding one month. Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 repealed only the words from "shall be of force" to the end, and No. 4 of 2024 s.2 renumbered the section and rewrote paragraphs (a) and (b). The quoted words therefore stood at October 2020 and applicable_to_matter_date should read true. Only the notarial-execution limb, which the map does not quote, is post-date. The subsection label "(1)" also comes from the 2024 renumbering. The provision can stay supporting, but the reason given for that role is wrong.

disagreements.researcher_position: The pre-2022 wording of rule (9) survives verbatim inside 31-2022/s16 but was left as a note in the research notes rather than made a provision, and PROV-M065-022 quotes the post-2022 text with applicable_to_matter_date false.
disagreements.verifier_position: Because that wording is quotable from the corpus, it should be a provision in its own right so that the identification point in question 1 rests on October 2020 text rather than on a post-date substitute. Added as PROV-M065-903. The lawyer should confirm that quoting an amending Act's recital of repealed words is an acceptable citation form for this benchmark.

unsupported_claims: None rejected. Every rule claim in both questions was traced to a provision whose excerpt says what the claim says. CL-M065-Q01-001 is the weakest: the excerpt it cites establishes that a lease exceeding one month falls within Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, but the words that impose the writing-and-notarial-attestation requirement are in the part of the section rewritten in 2022 and are not quotable at the matter date. The claim is left verified because the requirement is not in doubt and PROV-M065-008 is supporting only, but the lawyer should see the point.
temporal_issues: Confirmed against the amending Acts themselves rather than the event list: No. 47 of 2011 amends rule (16)(a) and rule (26); No. 13 of 2013 amends section 27, not section 31; No. 31 of 2022 s.16 amends rules (3), (4), (5), (6), (9), (14), (16), (17), (20)(b), (20)(e), (20)(g) closing words, (30) and inserts (7A), (15A), (20)(h), (30A) and repeals (27); No. 6 of 2024 s.3 amends rules (5), (7A), (9), (15A), (17), (20)(g), (26), (29), (30) and repeals (10). Rules (2), (8), (12), (18), (21), (22), (23), (24), (25), (28) and rule (20)(a), (c), (d), (f) are untouched throughout, so the researcher's temporal notes on those are right.
PROV-M065-008 is marked not applicable to the matter date when the quoted words in fact stood at October 2020. Recorded as a disagreement.

The gold prose for M065-Q02 recites the substance of rule (20)(b) and (e) in their 2022 form (identification by national identity card, bio-page of the passport or driving licence; details of any cheque, pay order, bank draft or banker's cheque) inside a rule statement addressed to an October 2020 matter. The conclusion says plainly that those two items are 2022 wording and that the question is blocked, so the prose is not misleading in context, but if this answer is ever unblocked the two items must be rewritten from a point-in-time 2020 text rather than trimmed.

PROV-M065-021 (rule (14)) and PROV-M065-022 (rule (9)) are post-date text carried as supporting for question 1. No claim relies on either, which is the right handling; the risk is that a later editor treats the corporate-seal duty in rule (14) as October 2020 law.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Notaries Ordinance s.2, the source of the notary's area of authority, was missing and is added as PROV-M065-904.

Section 4A, which deems a warrant for a judicial division to authorise practice in the notary's judicial zone, is mentioned in PROV-M065-003's temporal note but is not a provision. It is the provision that settles that a Colombo warrant does not reach Galle. Not added, because rule (22) with section 2 already carries the point, but the lawyer may want it cited.

Section 32(1) excludes rules (20), (23), (24), (25) and (26) for five classes of deed (powers of attorney for use out of Sri Lanka, deeds solely affecting foreign property, government stock transfers, transfers of stock in companies without a Sri Lankan registered office, and ships' notices of protest). A lease of a warehouse in Galle falls into none of them, so the exclusion does not bite, but the map nowhere records that the exclusion was considered.
Rule (27), in force at the matter date and squarely about part-executed deeds, was missing and is added as PROV-M065-901.
Section 32(2)(ii) was missing from question 2 and is added as PROV-M065-902.

Rule (16)(a) (description of the land) and rule (17) (search of the land registry before drawing a deed affecting land) bear on Ruwan Perera's drafting but not on execution or attestation contents, so their absence is defensible. Rule (17) in particular had different wording at October 2020.

Section 33 (no invalidity for a defect of form) and section 34 (penalties for breach of the section 31 rules) were considered and rejected by the researcher; I agree, neither question asks about consequences of non-compliance.
case_law_dependence: None. Both answers are worked entirely from the Notaries Ordinance, the Companies Act and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, and no judgment, reported citation or Roman-Dutch doctrine appears in either draft. statute_only is correct for both.

duplicate_or_leak_issues: No duplication between the two questions' provision sets beyond PROV-M065-001 and PROV-M065-009, which genuinely serve both (rule (25) is the entry point for the mechanics in question 1 and for the first notary's heavier duty in question 2).

The corpus text of rule (21) contains a transcription artefact, a capitalised "With" in "authenticated by the notary With the initial letters of his name". The excerpt stops before it, so nothing is quoted wrongly, but the corpus should be corrected.

Form E of the Second Schedule, which rule (21) requires the attestation to follow, is not a corpus section. The map records this as a corpus gap, correctly; it is the second half of what question 2 is really asking for.

Is it acceptable, for this benchmark, to cite an amending Act's recital of the words it repeals (PROV-M065-903, from Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(6)) as the matter-date text of the principal enactment?
